ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier) Articles L.561-1 to L.561-59 and R.561-1 et seq. implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended by Directive (EU) 2018/843; French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) Articles R.123-221 et seq. governing the UBO declaration (introduced by Ordinance n 2016-1635 and Decree n 2017-1094, now integrated in the Registre National des Entreprises under Law n 2019-486 / PACTE); Law n 2020-1672 establishing the Anti-Fraud National Register (REGIF); INPI guichet unique regulations for RNE filings; supervisory jurisprudence of the CJEU Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20 (Luxembourg Business Registers) restricting public access to UBO registers.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access with restricted legitimate-interest access: the UBO declaration is filed with the RNE/Greffe and visible to the French FIU (Tracfin), the tax administration, ACPR-supervised institutions, notaries, bailiffs and authorized third parties demonstrating a legitimate interest; unrestricted public access has been suspended following the CJEU C-37/20 ruling of 22 November 2022.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each shareholder and of the appointed gérant (manager), being the primary UBO identification document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the shareholder's or manager's country of residence (Ministry of Interior, police or civil registry authority); copy certified by a notary, by the issuing consulate or by a court-certified translator
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent Apostille authority of the issuing state where that state adheres to the 1961 Apostille Convention; otherwise French consular legalization at the Resident French Embassy or Consulate. A certified French translation by a traducteur assermenté must accompany the authenticated document for French RNE filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification and structural inspections from the local fire brigade, along with occupational health and safety clearance from the Labour Inspectorate.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP); central portal: impots.gouv.fr; online professional space: 'Espace professionnel' / 'Gérer mon entreprise'.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a French SARL, the statutory tax identification number is the SIREN obtained from INPI/Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés at incorporation; the intra-community VAT number is obtained by filing CERFA no. 3310-CA (or, for non-EU operators, CERFA no. 15738) with the local service des impôts des entreprises (SIE) or the DGFiP central office; non-EU entities without an establishment in France must also appoint an accredited fiscal representative to complete the VAT registration procedure and submit periodic returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: French law does not provide a check-the-box regime. A SARL is by default subject to corporation tax (impôt sur les sociétés) at entity level; a qualifying small SARL (SARL de famille or eligible SME) may elect for pass-through treatment under Article 239 bis AA of the French General Tax Code, in which case profits are taxed at member level; ATAD hybrid mismatch elections are limited to the specific carve-outs and disclosure forms required under Article 212 bis CGI.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual taxable turnover for goods and EUR 37,500 for services under the domestic franchise en base; however, for a VAT-established entity such as a French SARL, registration is generally mandatory when carrying on a taxable activity, and non-established foreign suppliers have no de minimis threshold – they are registrable from the first taxable euro unless reverse-charge or special scheme applies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates B2B electronic invoicing and e-reporting through the national Portail Public de Facturation (PPF) or a certified Private Dematerialization Platform (PDP) with API connectivity; phased implementation starts on 1 September 2026; invoices must be transmitted electronically within the statutory deadlines and e-reporting data sent to DGFiP; France does not operate a real-time fiscal-clearance or digital-stamping model akin to Italy or Latin American jurisdictions, but the PPF/PDP pipeline provides periodic validated transmission and audit-ready data.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: International transport of goods to non-EU destinations and related loading, unloading, handling, or ancillary services directly connected to such exports are zero-rated under Article 262-1-II of the French CGI when the service provider is a taxable person established in France and possesses documentary evidence proving physical export from the EU; intra-Community transport is not zero-rated but is generally subject to reverse charge in the destination Member State.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU/EBE) accepted by French customs or exit summary declaration
Proof of physical exit from the European Union (electronic exit confirmation or customs-endorsed transit document)
Commercial invoice with Incoterms, EORI number, and description of goods and destinations
Transport contract and consignment waybill (single airway bill or CMR consignment note) for the international shipment
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT confirmation, or bank statement proving receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DGFiP and French customs can retrospectively claw back improperly claimed zero-rating with VAT assessment, 0.40% monthly late-payment interest, and administrative penalties of 40% for intentional misstatement or 80% for organized fraud or abuse of right; false customs declarations may trigger separate customs fines, seizure of goods, and criminal liability for senior management; documentary discrepancies in the outward shipment trail are treated as an audit red flag.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France) in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (DG Trésor) within the Ministère de l'Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté Industrielle et Numérique; sole monetary and prudential authority plus balance-of-payments statistical control; the Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution (ACPR) supervises banks and fintech EMIs for AML/KYC enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro (EUR) is fully convertible for current account transactions under Articles 63 and 64 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier). France applies no general exchange-control licensing for ordinary commercial payments in EUR or freely convertible foreign currencies. Capital account movements are liberalized within the EU/EEA; outward transfers of funds to non-EU/EEA persons are unrestricted except for: (i) mandatory anti-money laundering reporting, (ii) EU sanctions and asset freezes, (iii) restrictions on transfers involving non-cooperative jurisdictions (FATF black/grey lists), and (iv) the foreign-investment screening regime (IEF – Investissements Étrangers en France) under Articles L151-1 to L151-8 for investments in sensitive sectors; courier/logistics is not a protected sector unless it touches dual-use or data-security activities. Profit remittance by a SARL to a foreign parent is lawful without dividend pre-clearance; only the standard withholdings/distribution formalities apply. Current-account convertibility is therefore complete; capital-account convertibility is effectively complete outside defense, dual-use, and personally sensitive data activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: France imposes NO mandatory surrender of export proceeds. Export receipts in EUR or foreign currencies may be retained, held in foreign-currency bank accounts (comptes devises), or converted freely. Statutory reporting applies instead of surrender: all cross-border transfers to/from non-EU countries exceeding EUR 10,000 must be declared by the paying/receiving bank to French customs and the DGDDI (Direction Générale des Douanes et Droits Indirects) under Article L152-1 of the Code monétaire et financier. Additionally, the Banque de France requires balance-of-payments (BOP) statistical filing for direct investment transactions where cumulative flows exceed EUR 15 million annually per counterparty/transaction; the SARL must also maintain an accurate register of receivables and FX positions, but no conversion ratio or repatriation timeline applies to express-courier export invoices.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.onboarding_viability_tier: Medium (investment-bank focus; not primary for SME SARL)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate. French-licensed fintech EMIs (établissements de monnaie électronique) — e.g., Qonto, Shine, and international EMIs passporting into France (Revolut Business, N26 Business) — are viable for day-to-day operations, SEPA/instant credit transfer collections, and multi-currency settlement up to the degree they offer physical or virtual FX accounts; however, they are legally prohibited from accepting demand deposits tied to credit creation, cannot grant overdrafts or working-capital credit, and generally do not execute export-proceeds reporting for customs/Banque de France. An EMI account is acceptable as a secondary operating rail but insufficient as the sole treasury and clearing hub for an international express-courier SARL. The compliance risk-tier of the courier industry (Medium_Risk_Enhanced) means ACPR-regulated EMIs will additionally apply enhanced due diligence; onboarding headroom improves if the SARL holds its principal account at a Tier-1 bank and uses the EMI solely for POS/acquirer settlement. Offshore digital EMIs domiciled outside the EEA are Non-Viable for principal treasury functions because they lack ACPR authorization to hold French SARL funds, cannot offer IBAN-based SEPA clearing, and create tax transparency risks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law permits fully remote onboarding for legal entities using a qualified electronic signature and a video-identification process that complies with Articles R561-5-2 to R561-5-4 of the Code monétaire et financier and EBA Guidelines on remote customer due diligence. In practice, Tier-1 French commercial banks (BNP Paribas, Société Générale, CIC) nearly always require at least one physical interview with the legal representative or a notarized apostilled power of attorney (procuration) appointing a resident manager/agent to appear on site; the physical presence mandate also intensifies when the SARL's beneficial owner (associé gérant) is a non-resident, when the corporate group is newly formed, or when the account is designated for capital escrow. A pragmatic blueprint: (i) open the capital-escrow account in person or via a resident company secretary holding a notarized power of attorney; (ii) complete remote video authentication only for secondary operational accounts; and (iii) prepare a bilingual legalized corporate file (statuts, Kbis, IBAN forecast, UBO registry extract) to convert the interview into a formality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Front-line red flag: high-value cross-border courier payments initiated from sanctioned, FATF grey-listed, or tax-blacklisted territories in the route network.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Furnish (1) a complete routing map of origin/destination countries excluding sanctioned entities; (2) EU/OFAC/ONU sanctions-screening certificates for counterparties and final beneficiaries; (3) shipment-level commercial invoices and airway bills matching payment amounts; and (4) a written AML compliance policy with client-onboarding KYC files for contract customers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner is a non-EU resident holding ultimate control of the SARL, creating an unfalsifiable UBO identification obstacle for bank compliance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver (1) updated RCS UBO registry extract (registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) not older than 30 days; (2) legalized and apostilled passport copies; (3) source-of-wealth and source-of-funds report for each UBO; (4) audited or accountant-certified financial statements of the parent entity; and (5) a signed declaration of origin of the initial capitalization funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-heavy or crypto-adjacent settlement patterns — courier digital payments or COD (cash-on-delivery) flows exceeding bank thresholds without predicate documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit (1) banking statements evidencing predominantly cashless receipts (credit card POS, SEPA Direct Debit, commercial ACH); (2) a formal corporate policy prohibiting cash settlements above EUR 1,000 per transaction; (3) a certified monthly reconciliation of COD collections with courier manifests; and (4) an independent third-party audit opinion confirming segregation of client money and sub-processor settlement accounts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Director/associé identity verification failure where the gérant carries a PEP (politically exposed person) status or resides in a disputed jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compile (1) documented majority-physical-present interview protocol; (2) consolidated PEP screening file with relationship explanation, risk rating, and annual review commitment; (3) apostilled birth certificate, passport, and sworn translation; (4) a French domiciliation certificate for the registered office; and (5) an escalation and transaction-monitoring plan approved by the bank's compliance officer.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity and shareholder-loan inflows into the French SARL must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with a remitter reference explicitly indicating 'APPPORT / CAPITAL SOCIAL' or 'COMPTE COURANT D'ASSOCIÉ', and must include the SARL's IBAN and the corporate purpose code compatible with the Banque de France BOP statistical coding, primarily: 'Investissement Direct Étranger (IDE)' – code 6C1P for equity participation and 6C1Q for shareholder loans, or for advances: 'Crédit Commercial' codes. The capital subscription must be deposited in accordance with Article L223-7 of the French Commercial Code: funds are either placed in an escrow account at a French bank, or, for an SARL, remitted directly to the manager against a receipt and presented with the 'attestation du dépositaire' to the RCS registrar. The installing bank must complete: (i) beneficiary-side verification of source of funds; (ii) automatic reporting to customs where inbound amount exceeds EUR 10,000 from a non-EU country; and (iii) quarterly BOP reporting to the Banque de France via the ORME (Observatoire pour la Réforme du Marché des Entreprises) portal if the inbound cumulative direct investment exceeds EUR 15 million. For amounts below EUR 15 million, no prior authorization is required; the sole obligation is bank-held record-keeping and, if the counterparty is a listed 'non-cooperative' jurisdiction, the bank will apply a mandatory procuration/registration blockade under Article R152-1 of the Code monétaire et financier.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements are stratified as follows: (A) primary rail – SWIFT MT103 for all non-SEPA cross-border beneficiary payments, with mandatory structured reference (41A order, 50K ordering customer, 72 remittance info) and full sanctions/beneficiary-account-name verification; (B) EU/EEA operations – SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) using IBAN-to-IBAN rails, no FX cost, execution within T+0/T+1; (C) documentary settlement – Commercial Letter of Credit (USance L/C 30–90) confirmed by CACIB or HSBC Continental Europe when the SARL imports courier technology/sorting equipment or settles high-value subcontracting receivables; (D) ACH Direct as secondary national French collection rail for recurring domestic invoices via SEPA Direct Debit Core, not for international clearing; and (E) cheque/trésorerie optional rail discretional on the bank. All outward disbursements require treasury management standing instructions such that every MT103 covers the courier service invoice reference, country routing, and the 4-digit DGDDI purpose code to prevent bank rejections and to preserve corporate VAT/export-compliance audit chain.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX Forwards (forwards de change) up to 12 months tenor against EUR, executed under standard ISDA/FEBI conventions with a French credit institution, fully documented under EMIR with trade reporting where the collateral threshold is exceeded
FX Swaps (simples) – EUR/USD and EUR/GBP swap points quoting by BNP Paribas or Société Générale Global Markets, permissible for matching the courier settlement cycle without limitations on depth
Currency Options (Call/Put European-style) and order-driven options bought to hedge unexpected airborne/parcel volatile exposures; selling naked options not permitted against prudent treasury policy
Cross-Currency Swaps limited to fixed-floating EUR vs. USD/GBP maturities under 24 months for the financing of customs prefinancing and regional distribution hubs

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) admissible only as a fallback for secondary-currency exposure (e.g., emerging-market routes such as TRY, BRL, EGP) where an onshore deliverable forward is functionally impossible; executed back-to-back with a top-tier regional bank and subject to Banque de France statistical declaration if the notional exceeds reporting thresholds

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual financial statements approval and filing (dépôt des comptes annuels)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registry of the Commercial Court)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year end; e.g., 30 June for 31 December year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil fine up to EUR 1,500; late filing suspends dividend distributions; failure for two consecutive years may result in judicial dissolution

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (Liasse fiscale, form 2065-SD)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year companies, by the 2nd working day after 1 May; for other fiscal year ends, within 3 months of close (extended to 4 months for electronic filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late filing penalty, increased to 40% after formal notice, plus monthly late-payment interest of 0.2%; any unreported basis subject to additional penalty

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual actualisation of the register of beneficial owners (UBO/DBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in ownership or control; annual internal verification at the ordinary general meeting that accepts the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fine up to EUR 225,000 and imprisonment for deliberate non-disclosure; refusal of registration of the instrument reflecting the transfer

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual business premises tax declaration and payment (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises, CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP – Service des Impôts des Entreprises (SIE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: CFE payment due by 15 December of each year; initial declaration form 1447-C must be filed by 31 December in the year of business creation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment interest and 10% penalty; if no declaration, the tax base may be increased by 50%

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit (Commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory if the SARL exceeds at least two of the following three thresholds at financial year-end: total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000; net turnover excluding VAT EUR 8,840,000; average permanent headcount 50. Mandatory also for companies controlling or being controlled by other entities, or for subsidiaries of a group that produces consolidated accounts.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP under Règlement ANC n° 2014-03, in accordance with Articles L.123-12 et seq. of the French Commercial Code; IFRS is permitted only for consolidated annual accounts of listed public-interest entities, not for standalone SARL financial statements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France requires the UBO declaration to be filed with the RCS upon incorporation and updated within 30 days of any modification of beneficial ownership or control. There is no standalone annual UBO filing, but each year at the ordinary general meeting approving the accounts, the managing director must confirm the UBO list is accurate and record any share transfers in the share transfer register. Failure to update the UBO register prevents legal effect of the transfer and exposes officers to penalties.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors and Managing Officers
Register of Meetings and Written Decisions (Registre des décisions et minutes)
Share Transfer Register (Registre de mouvements de titres)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: $60 – $350 per annum (depending on provider and whether a physical French registered office or virtual address is used)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: $4,500 – $12,000 for a typical express courier SARL (mandatory or voluntary certified audit fee)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: R&D tax credit (up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses) and accelerated depreciation allowances

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Tax Return (Form 1201) filed electronically through the French tax authority portal at impots.gouv.fr
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Three months after the end of the fiscal year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 - Taxable income before deductions and exemptions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit before any deductions, exemptions or tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Base amount used to calculate any applicable withholding taxes on distributions to non-resident shareholders

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductions including R&D tax credit and other incentives
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents may apply for treaty relief by submitting supporting documentation and Tax Residency Certificate

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of €250 to €10,000 or 0.5% to 5% of annual turnover, plus daily surcharge of €20 per day (maximum €200 per day); willful non-compliance may result in criminal prosecution

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Submit Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) and request for DTA benefits to the French tax authorities via impots.gouv.fr or the Mutual Agreement Procedure
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 0% to 10% (treaty-dependent); Interest: 0% to 25% (treaty-dependent, frequently reduced to 0% for related-party debt)

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: €50 million for local file; €250 million for master file
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Compliance with France's Economic Substance Law (aligned with EU Directive); requires local operational and managerial substance for qualifying activities, particularly relevant for cross-border services like courier operations

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately misstating income, expenses, or assets to reduce tax liability
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal penalty of up to 5 years imprisonment and fines up to 80% of the evaded tax (or higher in aggravated cases)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal criminal liability, including imprisonment, fines, and disqualification from office

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to File or Late Filing
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-submission or delayed submission of the annual corporate tax return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine ranging from €250 to €10,000 or 0.5% to 5% of turnover, plus daily penalties of €20 per day
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior directors can be held personally liable for fines and, in cases of gross negligence, criminal sanctions

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Engaging in transactions without arm's length pricing or failing to maintain required TP documentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalties up to 500% of the tax adjustment or specific TP penalties of €10,000 to €100,000 per infringement
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve non-compliant arrangements may face personal restitution orders and civil liability

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company or Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining a shell entity without sufficient economic substance or using it to shift profits artificially
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal sanctions including fines up to €1 million and imprisonment for serious cases
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil leading to personal civil and criminal liability, including travel bans in extreme cases

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to conduct proper KYC, CDD, or suspicious transaction reporting for cross-border courier services
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines up to €1 million or 5% of annual turnover, plus potential criminal prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managers may incur personal fines and imprisonment for willful AML breaches
